basicPropertyValues.val: An ontology of human taste perception: the qualities people perceive when they taste, and the tasting events in which they report them.
Developed at BioHackathon 2026, Matsuyama, Japan. The HTO prefix is not yet registered with the OBO Foundry, so HTO PURLs do not resolve.

definition.val: A cinchona alkaloid that is cinchonidine in which the hydrogen at the 6-position of the quinoline ring is substituted by methoxy.
An optically active form of glutamic acid having <small>L</small>-configuration.
A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.
An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.
A trimethylxanthine in which the three methyl groups are located at positions 1, 3, and 7. A purine alkaloid that occurs naturally in tea and coffee.
A disaccharide derivative that consists of hesperetin substituted by a 6-O-(α-L-rhamnopyranosyl)-β-D-glucopyranosyl moiety at position 7 via a glycosidic linkage.
A disaccharide derivative that is (S)-naringenin substituted by a 2-O-(α-L-rhamnopyranosyl)-β-D-glucopyranosyl moiety at position 7 via a glycosidic linkage.
A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms.

A member of the class of thioureas that is thiourea in which one of the hydrogens is replaced by a phenyl group. Depending on their genetic makeup, humans find it either very bitter-tasting or tasteless. This unusual property resulted in N-phenylthiourea being used in paternity testing prior to the advent of DNA testing.
A pyrimidinethione consisting of uracil in which the 2-oxo group is substituted by a thio group and the hydrogen at position 6 is substituted by a propyl group.
A specialized cell involved in gustatory sensory perception.
A whole fruit of a pomelo tree (Citrus maximus)
A hesperidium fruit of a citrus plant (Citrus).
A hesperidium fruit of a grapefruit tree (Citrus x paradisi).
A hesperidium fruit of a mandarin orange tree (Citrus reticulata).
A hesperidium fruit of a yuzu plant (Citrus junos)

nodes.lbl: detection of chemical stimulus involved in sensory perception of bitter taste

definition.val: The series of events required for a bitter taste stimulus to be received and converted to a molecular signal.

Note that, in addition to forming the root of the biological process ontology, this term is recommended for the annotation of gene products whose biological process is unknown. When this term is used for annotation, it indicates that no information was available about the biological process of the gene product annotated as of the date the annotation was made; the evidence code 'no data' (ND), is used to indicate this.
Combining with soluble compounds to initiate a change in cell activity. These receptors are responsible for the sense of taste.
Combining with soluble bitter compounds to initiate a change in cell activity. These receptors are responsible for the sense of bitter taste.

The series of events required for an organism to receive a gustatory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Gustation involves the direct detection of chemical composition, usually through contact with chemoreceptor cells. This is a neurological process.
The series of events required to receive a bitter taste stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.
The series of events required to receive a salty taste stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.
The series of events required to receive a sour taste stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.
The series of events required to receive a sweet taste stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

The series of events required to receive an umami taste stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Umami taste is the savory taste of meats and other foods that are rich in glutamates. This is a neurological process.
A G protein-coupled receptor activity that is responsible for the sense of bitter taste.
A decreased ability to perceive flavor.
A distortion of the sense of taste, often characterized by the sensation of a metallic taste.
A rare condition that is characterized by a complete loss of taste function of the tongue.
A planned process in which a human taster orally samples a stimulus and reports one or more perceived taste qualities.
A role borne by a person in virtue of taking part in a tasting event as the person doing the tasting.
A material entity presented to a taster to be tasted.
A taste stimulus consisting of a single chemical compound presented at a stated concentration in order to calibrate or classify a taster.
An information content entity recording that one taster perceived one perceptual taste quality in one stimulus on one occasion.
A scalar measurement datum recording how strong a perceived taste quality was, on a stated scale.
A scalar measurement datum recording how much a taster liked or disliked a stimulus, on a stated scale.
An information content entity specifying the permitted values and anchors used to record a rating.
A scalar measurement datum recording the lowest concentration of a tastant at which a taster reliably detects that something differs from the blank.
A scalar measurement datum recording the lowest concentration of a tastant at which a taster reliably names the quality correctly.
An organism trait classifying a person by their sensitivity to a reference bitter tastant, conventionally propylthiouracil.
A taster status in which the person reports no bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.
A taster status in which the person reports moderate bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.
A taster status in which the person reports intense bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.
An information content entity recording the pair of TAS2R38 haplotypes carried by a person, each haplotype being the combination of the amino acid states at positions 49, 262 and 296.
An information content entity recording an assertion about a person's genotype at a locus relevant to taste perception.
A planned process comprising the tasting events performed by one or more tasters on one occasion under one protocol.
A process performed between tasting events in order to reduce carry-over of taste from the previous stimulus.
An information content entity stating what the taster was able to know about the identity of the stimulus at the time of tasting.
A scalar measurement datum recording perceived intensity as a function of time since the stimulus entered the mouth.
An information content entity recording a property of a taster that is known to alter taste perception and that should be accounted for when analysing their ratings.
A taste confounder recording that the taster currently uses tobacco.
A taste confounder recording that the taster recently had an upper respiratory infection, including a recent loss of smell.
A taste confounder recording that the taster has reduced salivary flow.
A taste confounder recording that the taster takes a medication with a documented taste-distortion side effect.
A scalar measurement datum recording a value a taster reported on a stated scale, whether of a perceived quality's intensity or of liking.
A quality of a material entity that is realised when a human perceiver tastes that entity.
A perceptual taste quality for which a dedicated class of human taste receptor and a dedicated transduction pathway are established.
The basic taste quality typically elicited by sucrose and other sugars, transduced by the TAS1R2 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.

comments: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

definition.val: The basic taste quality typically elicited by citric acid and other acids, transduced by proton-sensitive channels of taste receptor cells.

comments: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

definition.val: The basic taste quality typically elicited by sodium chloride. The epithelial sodium channel is implicated in its transduction, and is well supported in rodents, but a substantial part of human salt taste is amiloride-insensitive and the channel's role in humans remains contested.

comments: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

definition.val: The basic taste quality typically elicited by quinine and by many plant alkaloids and glycosides, transduced by the TAS2R receptor family.

comments: Mapped to PATO:0002474 by skos:exactMatch in mappings/hto-pato.sssom.tsv.

definition.val: The basic taste quality typically elicited by L-glutamate and by certain ribonucleotides, transduced by the TAS1R1 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.

comments: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

definition.val: A perceptual taste quality that has been proposed as basic but for which receptor or transduction evidence remains contested.

comments: Grouped separately so that including these terms does not commit a user of HTO to the claim that they are basic tastes.

definition.val: The candidate taste quality elicited by non-esterified fatty acids, proposed under the name oleogustus and distinct from the texture of fat.
The candidate taste quality described as mouthfulness, continuity and thickness, elicited by certain gamma-glutamyl peptides acting on the calcium-sensing receptor.
The candidate taste quality elicited by certain metal salts and reported as a side effect of some medications.
The candidate taste quality elicited by calcium salts, reported as chalky and somewhat bitter.
The candidate taste quality elicited by oligomeric glucose polymers independently of sweetness.
A bitterness distinguished by the chemical class of the compound that elicits it and, where known, by the receptor that detects it.
The bitterness elicited by compounds bearing a thiourea group, notably phenylthiocarbamide and propylthiouracil, detected by TAS2R38.

comments: The quality whose perception varies most sharply between people.

definition.val: The bitterness elicited by limonoid triterpenoids, notably limonin, which forms from a tasteless precursor after citrus fruit is juiced.
The bitterness elicited by flavanone glycosides, notably naringin, characteristic of grapefruit and pomelo.
The bitterness elicited by plant alkaloids such as quinine and caffeine.
The bitterness elicited by hydrophobic amino acids and by peptides rich in them, prominent in protein hydrolysates and aged cheese.
A quality perceived in the mouth through the trigeminal nerve rather than through taste receptor cells, recorded alongside taste by sensory panels.

comments: Not a taste sensu stricto. Included because panels record it and because astringency is central to citrus assessment.

definition.val: The chemesthetic quality of drying, roughening and puckering in the mouth, elicited by tannins and other polyphenols binding salivary proteins.

comments: CHEBI:74783 astringent exists but denotes a chemical role, not a perceptual quality.

definition.val: The chemesthetic quality of burning or stinging, elicited by capsaicinoids, piperine and allyl isothiocyanate.
The chemesthetic quality of coolness in the absence of a temperature change, elicited by menthol and related compounds.
The chemesthetic quality of vibration or numbness, elicited by alkylamides such as sanshool.

The chemesthetic quality elicited by dissolved carbon dioxide, arising from two distinct routes: conversion of carbon dioxide by carbonic anhydrase 4 on sour-sensing taste cells, and a separate trigeminal contribution.
A perceptual taste quality defined by when it appears or how long it persists relative to the stimulus entering the mouth.
The temporal taste quality of how long after the stimulus enters the mouth a taste is first perceived.
The temporal taste quality of a taste that persists after the stimulus has been swallowed or expectorated.
An aftertaste that is bitter in quality.
A bitterness that is absent or weak when the stimulus is first tasted and appears or strengthens over subsequent minutes to hours.

comments: Characteristic of citrus juice, where limonin forms after juicing.

definition.val: The temporal taste quality of a perceived intensity declining during continued exposure to an unchanging stimulus.
A quality of a stimulus consisting in how much a perceiver likes or dislikes tasting it, as distinct from what they perceive.
The hedonic taste quality of being pleasant to taste for a given perceiver.
The hedonic taste quality of being unpleasant to taste for a given perceiver, whether innately or through learning.

A rating scale running from zero to one hundred with quasi-logarithmically spaced verbal anchors from barely detectable to strongest imaginable sensation of any kind, permitting comparison of intensities across people.
A rating scale running from zero to one hundred with verbal anchors referring to the strongest imaginable taste sensation rather than to any sensation.
A rating scale with nine categories running from dislike extremely to like extremely, used to record liking.
A rating scale on which the taster marks a point on an unstructured line of stated length, conventionally one hundred millimetres.
A rating scale with categories running from far too little to far too much about a stated attribute, centred on just about right.
An assay in which a taster places a filter paper impregnated with propylthiouracil on the tongue and reports the bitterness, used to assign taster status.
A generically dependent continuant that is about some thing.
A scalar measurement datum is a measurement datum that is composed of two parts, numerals and a unit label.
A measurement datum is an information content entity that is a recording of the output of a measurement such as produced by a device.
The sensitivity toward of a sensory perception of taste.
The quality of a sensory perception of sweet taste.
The quality of a sensory perception of bitter taste.
The quality of a sensory perception of sour taste.
The quality of a sensory perception of salty taste.
The quality of a sensory perception of umami taste.
A planned process that has the objective to produce information about a material entity (the evaluant) by examining it.
A document with a set of printed or written questions with a choice of answers, devised for the purposes of a survey or statistical study.
A dependent entity that inheres in a bearer by virtue of how the bearer is related to other entities
A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's possessing or displaying a distinctive feature in type or degree or effect or force.

Relational qualities are qualities that hold between multiple entities. Normal (monadic) qualities such as the shape of a eyeball exist purely as a quality of that eyeball. A relational quality such as sensitivity to light is a quality of that eyeball (and connecting nervous system) as it relates to incoming light waves/particles.
A process quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's magnitude of the temporal extent between the starting and ending point.
The temporal relation between the start of the process with respect to a reference process.
A flavor quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having an acrid, sharp, or disagreeable flavor.

Anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. The boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. In vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).
A muscular organ in the floor of the mouth.
A specialized receptor organ that is a collection of cells spanning the gustatory epithelium.
Any of the mushroom-shaped papillae, which have a single taste bud at the tip, located mostly on the dorsal anterior portion of the tongue.
Relates a tasting event to the person who performed the tasting.
Relates a tasting event to the material that was tasted.
Relates a taste percept assertion to the perceptual taste quality it reports.
Relates a taste percept assertion to the intensity value reported for it.
Relates a rating to the scale on which it was recorded.
Relates a tasting event to the liking score the taster gave the sample.
Relates a tasting event to the session in which it took place.
Relates a person to their assessed taster status.
Relates a person to a recorded assertion about their taste-related genotype.
Relates a taste stimulus to the food or beverage class it was prepared from.
Relates a taste stimulus to a chemical entity present in it that bears a taste quality.
Relates a perceptual taste quality to the biological process by which it is perceived.
Relates a perceptual taste quality to a receptor whose activation is established to contribute to perceiving it.
Relates a tasting event to a taste percept assertion produced in it.
Relates a taster status to a diplotype that commonly but not invariably produces it. This is a statistical association and deliberately not an equivalence.
Relates a person or a study group to the diplotype they carry, or that characterises them.
Relates a threshold datum to the perceptual taste quality whose detection or recognition it measures.
The numeric value of a rating on its stated scale.
The lowest value the scale admits.
The highest value the scale admits.
The position of this sample in the order presented to the taster, counting from one.
True when the taster could not identify the sample at the time of tasting.
The date on which a tasting session was held.
Minutes elapsed between preparing the stimulus and tasting it. Relevant where a quality develops after preparation, as limonoid bitterness does in citrus juice.
Definition source denoting a term authored by the HTO editors for this release rather than taken from a cited publication.
